# Slice boundary 1 of 3, kept by hand

`harness handoff` is slice 2 of this ticket, so the first boundary is written as a note,
which is the decision recorded in the clarify record at record 9. This is the pack, in the
shape the command will produce.

## Where the work stands

Stage tdd, attempt 1, records 1 to 12. Branch `claude/SEEN-104-cap-a-session-at-one-slice`,
slice 1 green and committed at af8d61e. The full suite is 358 tests, OK, in 81 seconds.

Slice 1, session identity and the slice-plan gate, is done: `[session]` in
`harness/thresholds.toml`, `harness/sessions.py`, the session in the record envelope with
`HARNESS_VERSION` at 2, `gates._slice_plan` with its two caps and the non-code exemption,
`slices` in `harness/templates/solution.json`, and `harness/tests/test_session_cap.py`.
RED at record 11 (6 failures, 8 errors), GREEN at record 12.

Records 13 onwards belong to slice 2, the handoff pack, its record and `status --brief`,
then slice 3, `budget`, the KPI figures, the sprint report row and the skill. Both are
planned in the solution record at record 10, with the files each touches.

## What this session cost

124,639 output tokens and 83 tool calls, against the 60,000 token budget this slice wrote
into `thresholds.toml`. Twice over, on the session that wrote the number.

Where it went: the clarify stage read eleven harness modules to answer what the ticket
touches, and `clarified` was read four times at 0.76 to 0.77 before Ruud recorded the
override at record 8. That is what a session pays to start a ticket cold, and it is the
case for the pack: the next session needs the ticket file, the solution record at record 10
and this note, and nothing else. It should not read `cli.py`, `kpi.py` or `report.py` until
slice 3 asks it to.

The figure is evidence for the budget rather than against it. The budget is what one
session should spend on one slice; this session spent it on a clarify stage, a solution
stage and a slice, which is what the cap exists to stop.

## The next command

`python3 harness/run.py status SEEN-104`, then slice 2: write the RED for the pack in
`harness/tests/test_session_cap.py`, `harness/run.py check SEEN-104 --phase red`, then
`harness/handoff.py` and the `handoff` command with `handoff` added to `paths.KINDS`.
